heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: The PhageFoundry collection contains 96 phages × 188 E. coli strains × 17,672 susceptibility pairs, sufficient for a 5-phage E. coli AIEC cocktail with 95 % strain coverage.

heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: The other 5 actionable Tier-A species are absent from phagefoundry_strain_modelling, so their phage availability relies solely on ref_phage_biology literature curation.

heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: The NB13 cocktail's 95 % coverage concerns 188 PhageFoundry-tested E. coli strains, not UC Davis patient isolates; patient applicability requires stool-isolate AIEC strain-resolution diagnostics.
quote: **NB13 5-phage cocktail covers PhageFoundry strains, not UC Davis patient isolates.** The 95 % strain-coverage figure is on the 188 PhageFoundry-tested *E. coli* strains. Per-patient applicability requires AIEC strain-resolution diagnostic on UC Davis patient stool isolates, which is queued in NB17 Near-term roadmap.
heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: HMP2 viromics has 80 % Unknown family classification, preventing linkage of most phage observations to target hosts.

heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: Improving HMP2 phage family resolution requires rerunning VirMAP/MARVEL with newer phage reference databases, which is out of scope.
quote: Family-resolution improvement requires VirMAP/MARVEL re-running with newer phage reference databases — out of scope.
heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: NB14 phageome associations with ecotype and diagnosis have modest effect sizes (max |ρ|≤0.18), whereas NB04e species-taxonomy effect sizes routinely have |CLR-Δ|>1.0.

heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: The report's 3-layer phage-evidence convergence relies on directional concordance rather than matched effect sizes across layers.
quote: The 3-layer phage-evidence convergence rests on directional concordance, not effect-size matching across layers.
heading: Pillar 4 limitations

text: The 23-patient UC Davis cohort supports cocktail exemplars/templates rather than statistically robust per-patient validation, and generalization requires multi-center validation.
